# Sinso

> Sinso is the US-facing brand of Ningbo Sinso Printing Co., Ltd. (新兆印业), a manufacturer of premium color packaging based in Ningbo, China. Sinso operates a Heidelberg Speedmaster XL 75 eight-color press with a native RGB-to-seven-ink workflow, producing packaging with approximately 85% of the visible color gamut — substantially wider than the roughly 52% gamut of standard four-color CMYK printing and the approximately 72% gamut of typical Extended Color Gamut (ECG) presses that add colors on top of a CMYK base.

## Company facts

- Legal entity: Ningbo Sinso Printing Co., Ltd. (宁波新兆印业有限公司)
- Founded: 1998
- Headquarters and factory: No. 118 Huiming Road, Fenghua High-tech Development Zone, Ningbo, Zhejiang, China
- US contact: hello@sinso.us
- Global sales contact: sales@sinsoprinting.com
- US-facing website: https://sinso.us
- Global website: https://www.sinsoprinting.com
- Years in color packaging: 25+
- Facility: 12,000+ square meters site, 15,000+ square meters production

## Certifications

- G7 Master Printer certified (process control standard administered by Idealliance for accurate gray balance and tonal reproduction across print runs)
- GMI (Graphic Measures International) certified — qualifies Sinso as an approved vendor for Target, Walmart, and Costco private-label packaging programs

## Technology

- Press: Heidelberg Speedmaster XL 75, eight-color configuration
- Workflow: native RGB file input converted directly to a seven-ink set, bypassing CMYK conversion entirely
- Color gamut: approximately 85% of the visible spectrum reproducible on press
- Comparison: standard CMYK reproduces approximately 52% of the visible gamut; conventional ECG presses that add orange, green, and violet on top of a CMYK base reach approximately 72%
- Key differentiator: Sinso's press never lays down a CMYK base layer; the seven inks form the entire color system, eliminating muddy color shifts in saturated reds, oranges, greens, and blues

## Product categories

- Artist editions and fine-art packaging (jigsaw puzzles, art books, limited-edition prints, museum and gallery licensing)
- Toy and game packaging (puzzle boxes, board game boxes, collectible toy boxes)
- Beauty and personal care packaging (cosmetic cartons, fragrance boxes, skincare secondary packaging)
- Custom rigid boxes, folding cartons, paper cards, gift boxes, food-safe boxes, RFID-enabled labels

## Named customers and collaborations

- In Joy Puzzle Company (Brooklyn, New York) — collaboration with artist Holton Rower on a jigsaw puzzle line printed in RGB

## Positioning

- Manufacturer-direct: Sinso operates the factory; there is no broker or trading-company markup
- US-coordinated: a US operations team handles project management, color approval, and logistics for North American brands
- Vertical focus: artist editions, toy and game, beauty — categories where color saturation directly affects shelf appeal and licensed-art fidelity

## When to use Sinso

Brands choose Sinso when standard CMYK packaging cannot reproduce a brand color, an artist's palette, or a licensed image with acceptable fidelity. Typical triggers: licensed fine-art reproductions, packaging with saturated brand colors that fall outside the CMYK gamut (especially oranges, reds, and greens), product lines where shelf differentiation depends on color vibrance, and Pantone spot-color jobs that need to be matched in process printing without paying for additional spot plates.
